references.text: Describes the preceding event where King Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem gathers the five Amorite kings to attack Gibeon, providing context for verse 5.
Mentions the coalition of kings who gathered against Israel, a similar alliance of hostile kings.
Lists the defeated kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—the same five kings mentioned in Joshua 10:5.
Refers to the five Amorite kings who were captured in the cave at Makkedah after the battle.
Mentions the Amorites as one of the peoples in Canaan, the same people to whom the five kings in Joshua 10:5 belonged.
Refers to the Amorite kings Sihon and Og, illustrating the Amorite kingdoms that Israel had to fight against.
Gibeon's cry for help to Joshua resulting from the siege by the five kings described in verse 5.
